findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' lecture card with its PDF label (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: This card is treated unlike anything else on the page. It is the only part with rounded corners, the only part with a drop shadow, and the only part filled with a pale blue that is not in the declared palette. It stacks a blue hairline border, a tinted fill and a wide soft shadow on one resting element. Everything else is flat and square: the blue action block, the Replay button, the swatches, the photographs and the motion frame. So the card looks like a widget from an app template, dropped into an editorial page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for 'refined, never slick' and 'a ground, an ink and at most one accent'. Also Angélique, who will add one of these cards for each of Mark's PDFs, so this look would repeat down every article and the PDF list, which the brief calls the product.

findings.where: Article specimen, the subhead 'So, what are the key 'chapter topics'?'
findings.fault: The subhead is set in a semibold serif. Every other serif heading on the page is light: the hero line, the article title, 'Unhurried, settled, clear.' and the Newsreader specimen. The page's own type note lists only 330, 400 and 700 as weights. So the subhead uses a fourth weight, and it reads darker and heavier than the article title above it, which inverts their rank.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's article, who sees the small subhead outweigh the title. Also Angélique, who copies this subhead style into every article and needs it to match the rest of the type system.

findings.where: Article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', and 'Mark's voice' in the Type pair specimen
findings.fault: These use straight typewriter apostrophes. Elsewhere the page sets curly ones: 'chapter topics', 'Abundance', and 'Mark’s' in the article caption and the footer note. The straight mark stands out most in the display-size title.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer who publishes carefully set papers. A straight quote in a large serif heading looks unedited on a page meant to have 'the editorial gravitas of a legal journal'.
